evidence.location: reports/current.md, complete 288 lines / 71692 characters; seven-program register, sections 2-6 and appendix
evidence.basis:
I read the complete task and complete frozen report, extending my former AIDD-U1 evidence scope to all seven programs, the stage comparison and partnership analysis. U1 is exactly equal to my previously assessed completed unit, and all six frozen discovery/clinical/registry source bodies are identical. Its original clinical article, Figure 2, Table 2, Reporting Summary and registry checks remain applicable; I did not substitute the unit pass for whole-report reading. The manuscript retains the observed-versus-imputed FVC populations and uncertainty, missingness, safety withdrawals, indication/formulation distinction and future phase-III status.

For the new scope I checked original DSP discovery and discontinuation accounts, EXS filings and trial records, REC-994's original screen, published phase-I abstract, dated stop and posted results, REC-4881's actual registry and primary corporate/SEC disclosures, the three baricitinib randomized trial publications and FDA notice, and halicin's original methods/results. Across these cases the report generally preserves the distinction between a computational proposal, tested mechanism, activity, safety and efficacy. It does not turn an abandoned program into success, a selected evaluable population into all enrolled participants, or a repurposed molecule into AI-originated chemistry. Its arithmetic is transparently derived from the disclosed counts; I inspected the existing calculation code and complete retained revised output, without rerunning either.

The dated partnership filings support the separation of candidate rights, platform IP, constrained partner-data use, experimental work, downstream development, received upfront cash and contingent milestone ceilings. The historical AI-native cohort is identified as an older selected cohort and does not supply an industry-wide causal success estimate. One necessary factual correction remains: DSP's number of tested compounds is described as a number of iterative feedback cycles. Specific access limits for one REC-4881 detail are recorded below rather than silently certified.

findings.basis: The final sentence says the team carried out 'hundreds of design–make–test iterations'. The cited Sumitomo scientific account states a two-week feedback cycle and 350 compounds synthesized and tested within less than one year; DSP-1181 was the 350th compound. These are different counting units. Nothing in that passage supports hundreds of sequential feedback cycles, and that wording inflates the iteration evidence underlying the speed claim. Replace it with hundreds of compounds synthesized/tested through the described two-week cycles, preserving the existing nomination endpoint and exclusion of safety evaluation. Original: sources/actual/AIDD06.txt lines 274-305, corresponding PDF p.4, https://www.sumitomo-chem.co.jp/english/rd/report/2021E_3.pdf. No new experiment or calculation is needed.

source_checks: Complete report read in bounded outputs 1-51, 52-100, 101-146, 147-189, 190-234, 235-288. Complete original case/assignment read. Source registry and actual-reading scope inspected; acquisition was not counted as reading. Supplied prior_required_findings is empty for this full-report assignment.

Reused my own AIDD-U1 v2, v3 and complete evidence readings. Current analysis/U1-rentosertib.md equals the old completed unit exactly. Current AIDD-A13, AIDD-R01W, AIDD-R02W, AIDD-S01, AIDD-S02 and AIDD03 frozen bodies equal the corresponding previously assessed bodies exactly. The full-report U1 section was nevertheless read. No other role's pass consulted.

DSP: original AIDD05 Jan.30,2020 sponsor announcement read; AIDD06 scientific account 154-252 and 274-311 read for model/chemistry/assay roles, agonism challenge, two-week loop, compound count and clock exclusion; AIDD08 transcript 232-249 confirms the Jan.31,2022 phase-I stop and unspecified unmet criterion. The concrete compound-versus-cycle mismatch is the finding above.

EXS21546: raw AIDD-R04/R05 protocol identification, status, enrollment, design and stop reason read. The 2022 20-F line 2115 independently supports nine months and 163 tested compounds (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1865408/000186540823000011/exai-20221231.htm). The 2023 20-F passages 603, 2137-2138, 2946, 4050-4060 and 6058-6059 support discontinued development, shared laboratory costs, separate services and changing ownership. Evotec's original target-engagement case lines 84-115 and original poster profile support its assay contribution, not clinical efficacy.

REC-994: AIDD-S14 original screen 222-245 supports CellProfiler/Analyst, 2100 compounds, matched 38-compound selections, nonoverlap, 7 versus 1 orthogonal validations and the mouse lesion result with P=.052. Published phase-I abstract at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38655895/ identifies tempol and healthy volunteers. The Sept.3,2024 primary disclosure https://ir.recursion.com/node/10581/pdf supports safety and exploratory MRI trends; AIDD-S20 original 189-192 documents nonsustained long-term trends and stop. Raw AIDD-R03W protocol/status, participant flow, entire CCMHI outcome and adverse-event population definitions read: 21/21/20 randomized, 19/20/18 part-1 completions, available-data CCMHI n=19/16/17 with LS means -5.8/-1.9/-7.8; combined active extension exposure is not a matched 12-month safety comparison.

REC-4881: raw AIDD-R06 protocol/status/design read. Recursion 2025 10-K discovery passages 613-642 and Takeda-license 1450-1466 substantiate prior TAK-733 chemistry, phenotypic APC rescue and conventional license economics. The Nov.2,2026 primary release supports 13/15, 47% median, 11/13, 26 safety participants and grade/discontinuation counts. The official 52-page earnings deck became readable at https://recursion.gcs-web.com/static-files/644d572d-a9f8-430a-9412-559e361c3dd5 and its SEC copy https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601830/000160183026000144/a3q26finaldeck_rxrx.htm. Relevant pp.16-17,21-22,24-25,29-31 establish 16 of 21 efficacy-evaluable, exposure/assessment criteria, time-specific missingness, excision add-back and the older 47-person annual-surveillance comparator. Those primary texts, not author notes, support the principal analysis. The precise 3/2 split of the five efficacy exclusions remains separately limited below.

Baricitinib: original AIDD-S24 correspondence 128-141 and S15 workflow passages establish human-guided knowledge-graph prioritization and existing-drug origin. S11 ACTT-2 333-356, S12 COV-BARRIER 188-195/229/497/506/639, and S13 RECOVERY 92-105 checked against denominators, interventions, recovery/mortality results, uncertainty and background treatment. The manuscript respects the failed COV-BARRIER primary endpoint and nominal mortality hierarchy. Original S25 FDA notice supports May10,2022 adult indication and the earlier separate EUA dates. No AI-attributed treatment effect or inferred royalty is claimed.

Halicin: original AIDD04 340-437, 726-816, 1295-1384 and 2140-2178 read. These substantiate 2335 deduplicated training molecules, hybrid directed message passing/ensemble, retrospective AUC .896, selected Hub top/bottom assay counts, prior SU3327 origin, experimental proton-gradient mechanism and Pseudomonas limitation, separate 107349233-molecule ZINC screen with 23 tested and 8 active against at least one species, and animal design/colonization limitations. The report keeps these selection and assay denominators separate.

Historical cohort: author-uploaded original Drug Discovery Today article methods and results at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380223979_How_successful_are_AI-discovered_drugs_in_clinical_trials_A_first_analysis_and_emerging_lessons read through lines 345-595, with figure caption excluding COVID programs. Its 21/24 and 4/10 historical completed cohorts are accurately dated and qualified. The existing calculations.py Wilson formula and complete calculations-results-revision-01.json were inspected; no calculation rerun.

Partnerships: Sanofi 2022 filed summary at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1865408/000110465922002006/tm222148d1_6k.htm lines 71-98 and filed contract clauses 20-23 (lines1306-1362) checked for rights, work allocation and redactions; Oct.15,2026 primary option release lines17-32 checked for candidate, future clinical start and payment/revenue categories. Roche Dec.2021 8-K lines98-115 checked for map/raw-image/program options, and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601830/000160183022000012/R26.htm confirms January2022 receipt. The Aug.5,2026 primary Genentech account lines2 and20-44 supports a validated target entering joint small-molecule work, not a named clinical drug.
access_limits: The CGA 17-page original PDF at https://ir.recursion.com/static-files/e3eb390d-76f3-4899-bb92-922eaaaf3c30 returned HTTP403 in direct/web retrieval; official indexed p.9 was accessible. The separate 52-page earnings deck and SEC copy provided independent primary confirmation of the core REC-4881 denominators and adjustments. I could not independently recover the specific statement that three of five excluded phase-II patients lacked any post-baseline endoscopy and two had insufficient exposure (report line147). This is an unverified detail in this review, not a demonstrated false statement or a reason to treat all REC-4881 evidence as absent. Author reading notes are not represented as my original reading.

PDF screenshot requests for REC-4881 returned access errors; no successful new visual review is claimed. EXAI2022 PDF was downloaded to this review folder but local extraction could not use the existing runtime; the equivalent original SEC 20-F text supplied the cited 9-month/163-compound evidence. Not every page of every referenced source or every clinical protocol was read; relevant original passages were read, and the entire current report was read.
